beats.say: Opened a suspicious file or sent data to the wrong person? Stay calm, the steps are short.
Opened the file? Turn off Wi-Fi and unplug the cable. Leave the computer on unless your procedure says otherwise.
Do not delete the file or the email: specialists learn from them what the attack did.
Report by phone, not from the infected computer. And never hide data sent to the wrong person.

scenes.title: You opened the file
scenes.intro: You opened the "Akt_imzala" attachment and allowed macros. Now strange things are happening.

body.text: A malicious macro was found in Akt_imzala.docm. Cleanup did not finish.

actions.label: Turn off Wi-Fi, unplug the cable
actions.feedback: Right. Off the network, the computer cannot spread the damage or send data out.

actions.label: Close and keep working
actions.feedback: The cleanup did not finish, so the program may still run. Every minute helps it spread.

actions.label: Delete the file
actions.feedback: Deleting destroys evidence and does not stop what already ran. Disconnect first.

body.text: Give TexKömək 24 remote access to clean it now.

actions.label: Allow remote access
actions.feedback: Remote access for an unknown app hands the attacker the whole computer. Help comes only from your own technical support.

actions.label: Decline
actions.feedback: Right. Do not try to clean it yourself; wait for security.

steps.say: The file is still in Downloads.

actions.label: Open again
actions.feedback: Every open can run the macro again. Leave the file alone.

actions.label: Delete
actions.feedback: Security needs the file to find out what it did. Do not delete it.

actions.label: Leave it as it is
actions.feedback: Right. The file is evidence; security will examine it safely.

body.text: Wi-Fi is off. Do you want to reconnect?

steps.say: You want to check your mail, but there is no network.

actions.label: Connect
actions.feedback: Stay offline until security says so: the program could encrypt your files or spread.

actions.label: Stay offline
actions.feedback: Right. Now call security from your phone and tell them what you opened.

question.prompt: The computer is infected and offline. Should you shut it down?

options.label: No, I leave it on unless our procedure says otherwise
options.feedback: Right. Traces in memory matter to the specialists.

options.label: Yes, I shut it down at once
options.feedback: Shutting down wipes traces in memory. Disconnecting already stops the spread.

options.label: No, I keep working on it
options.feedback: Working on an infected computer puts your passwords and files at risk.

scenes.explain: Disconnect, leave it on, report by phone. If your organisation's procedure differs, follow it.

scenes.prompt: You opened a suspicious file. Put the steps in order.

items.label: Disconnect the computer from the network
Say exactly what you opened and when
Change your passwords from another, clean device

scenes.explain: Never change passwords on the infected computer: the program could read the new ones too.

nodes.text: You sent the list to an outside address with the same name instead of your colleague Kamran. It holds citizens' names and phone numbers.

choices.label: I tell my manager and security right away
choices.feedback: Right. If personal data has leaked, the organisation must know in time.

choices.label: I tell nobody, maybe they won't open it
choices.feedback: If the leak stays hidden, the organisation cannot do anything to protect the citizens.

choices.label: I just ask the recipient to delete it, that's all
choices.feedback: Asking helps, but the organisation still needs to know about the leak.

nodes.text: Write politely to the recipient, ask them to delete the file and confirm it.
nodes.speaker: Security team
nodes.spoken: Write politely to the recipient, <breath> ask them to delete the file and confirm it.

choices.label: I write and forward the reply to the specialist
choices.feedback: Great. The written confirmation records that the leak was contained.

choices.label: I resend the file to Kamran and forget it
choices.feedback: Sending it to the right person is good, but the copy at the wrong address remains.

choices.label: I delete my sent email so no trace remains
choices.feedback: The sent email shows what went where and when. Keep it.

scenes.prompt: Did your colleague do the right thing?

body.text: I opened a strange file. I turned off Wi-Fi and I'm calling security now.

cards.explain: Right: disconnect first, then report by phone.

body.text: I opened the file, then deleted it. Nobody will know.

cards.explain: Deleting destroys the trail, and hiding gives the attack time.

body.text: A virus popped up, so I downloaded a free cleaner from the internet.

cards.explain: Installing tools yourself can wipe traces and bring in new malware.

body.text: I sent a document to an outside address by mistake. I told my manager and security right away.

cards.explain: Right. A quick report limits the damage.

points: Opened a bad file? Disconnect, leave it on unless your procedure says otherwise, report by phone.
Do not delete the file or the email, and do not try to clean up yourself.
Sent something to the wrong person? Do not hide it: tell your manager and security at once.
